title: Was the Garden of Eden in Iraq?
author: QUILL
notes: All Eden locations are proposals. Pishon/Gihon explicitly unidentified. Not-proven line in beat 11.

beats.text: Was the Garden of Eden in Iraq?
Genesis 2 names four rivers flowing out of Eden.
Two are real: the Tigris and the Euphrates, both flowing through Iraq today.
beats.say: Two are real: the TY-gris and the yoo-FRAY-teez, both flowing through Iraq today.

beats.text: The other two, Pishon and Gihon, were never securely identified.
beats.say: The other two, PIE-shon and GEE-hon, were never securely identified.

beats.text: The Pishon circles Havilah, where the gold is good.
beats.say: The PIE-shon circles HAV-ih-lah, where the gold is good.
beats.label: HAVILAH: GOOD GOLD

beats.text: One proposal points to dried riverbeds now buried beneath the Persian Gulf.
Another looks north, where the Tigris and Euphrates both begin.
beats.say: Another looks north, where the TY-gris and yoo-FRAY-teez both begin.

beats.text: So Eden sits at either end of the rivers, depending on who you ask.
beats.label: NORTH OR SOUTH?

beats.text: At al-Qurnah, where they meet, locals show a tree called Adam's.
beats.say: At al-KOOR-nah, where they meet, locals show a tree called Adam's.

beats.text: Some scholars link 'Eden' to the Sumerian word edin, meaning plain.
beats.say: Some scholars link Eden to the Sumerian word EH-din, meaning plain.
beats.label: EDIN = PLAIN?

beats.text: Plainly: Eden's location is not proven. These are proposals, not discoveries.
Real rivers, a lost garden, and no confirmed site.
Iraq, the Gulf, or Armenia: where would you search?
